findings.title: Item info card's equipped-offset row still shows unrevealed entad offsets/factors
findings.detail: ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats calls StatWorker.StatOffsetFromGear(req.Thing, stat) for every stat in the def's equippedStatOffsets with displayExcludesHidden unset, so Patch_StatOffsetFromGear adds the full total (hidden part included) and StatPart_Entad.TransformValue applies hidden statFactors. Meanwhile StatPart_Entad.ExplanationPart lists only revealed traits, so the row's final value differs from base + listed lines and gives the hidden trait away, which is the same leak the flag was added to stop on the pawn's gear line. Do not fix it by wrapping the whole SpecialDisplayStats iterator with the flag: other rows in that iterator call GetStatValue, which would push the flag into cached values. Scope it to this row only, or accept the leak deliberately.

findings.title: Hyperlink wrapper is correct for the lazy iterator
findings.detail: GetInfoCardHyperlinks is a yield iterator and RelevantGear (which calls GearAffectsStat) runs inside its MoveNext, so WithPawn setting explainingPawn around each MoveNext is what makes the postfix effective. This addresses the enumerator warning verify_patches prints for this target; no MethodType.Enumerator patch is needed.

findings.title: StatOffsetFromGear postfix still does a GetComp scan for nearly every worn apparel
findings.detail: EntadCompInjector adds CompProperties_Entad to most gear defs, so IsEntadGear is true for almost all apparel, and on every affected-stat evaluation the postfix does GetComp<CompEntad> (linear over comps) and WearerOffset allocates an empty Dictionary once per trait-less item. A null/empty activeTraits early-out in OffsetFrom (or at the top of WearerOffset) avoids both. Cheap already; this is just the remaining per-call cost.
